architectural_boundary.semantics_owner: existing applicable research governance; registry records identity and provenance relationships only
architectural_boundary.current_head_rule: derive the unique valid tip by replaying the complete current segment set; never trust a separately mutable head pointer

serialization.separators: comma and colon with no insignificant whitespace
serialization.unicode_normalization: NONE; exact valid Unicode string content is identity-bearing
serialization.arrays: order is identity-bearing unless an explicit sorted-set rule below applies

canonicalization.compatibility_note: Matches the existing ATDS stable-hash serialization pattern: json.dumps(sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'),ensure_ascii=False) then UTF-8 SHA-256, with additional fail-closed input restrictions defined here.

forbidden_as_decisive_identity: human-readable object name without immutable anchor

resolution_rules.git_blob: must resolve to the exact blob in the governed repository object database
resolution_rules.git_commit: must resolve to the exact commit in the governed repository object database
resolution_rules.event: must resolve to a validated event in an ancestor segment or, where explicitly allowed, the current segment
resolution_rules.relation: must resolve to a validated relation in an ancestor segment; current-segment relation-to-relation references are forbidden
resolution_rules.registry: must resolve to a validated ancestor registry segment

decisive_reference_grammar.existing_atds_object_rule: An existing ATDS object is decisively referenced through the immutable Git blob or commit containing its canonical persisted representation; this V0.1 does not create a second object-identity namespace.

field_rules.operator: non-empty string; identifies the declared human/process actor but grants no authority
field_rules.nature: non-empty string describing the research/observation event
field_rules.source_refs: array of decisive refs; lexicographically sorted; duplicate-free; may be empty for an explicitly unanchored human declaration
field_rules.period_start_utc: RFC3339 UTC whole-second string or null
field_rules.period_end_utc: RFC3339 UTC whole-second string or null
field_rules.period_pair_rule: both period boundaries null or both present; when present start <= end
field_rules.consultation_intensity: null or I1 or I2 or I3
field_rules.evidence_refs: array of decisive refs; lexicographically sorted; duplicate-free; may be empty only when no consultation intensity is asserted
field_rules.intensity_evidence_rule: if consultation_intensity is non-null evidence_refs must be non-empty
field_rules.i1_rule: if consultation_intensity is I1 information_accessed must be non-null and evidence_refs must be non-empty

event_record.id_rule: event_id = 'EVT-' + full 64-lowercase-hex SHA-256 of canonical identity_payload
event_record.mutation_rule: material correction to event_core creates a new EVENT_ID; existing event content is never rewritten under the same identity
event_record.temporal_rule: occurred_at_utc records declared occurrence time; durable recording order is established by registry/Git ancestry and is never backdated by occurred_at_utc

field_rules.source_ref: decisive reference; generalized from the conceptual SOURCE_EVENT_REF so all four adopted relation types can represent non-event sources without adding a new relation type
field_rules.basis_ref: required decisive reference supporting why this relation/status was recorded
field_rules.same_segment_relation_reference: FORBIDDEN for source_ref target_ref basis_ref and supersedes_relation_ref when the referenced object is a relation
field_rules.same_segment_event_reference: ALLOWED after all event identities in the segment validate
field_rules.adjudicated_gate: ADJUDICATED remains BLOCKED unless basis_ref is a git_blob included in a separately human-authorized adjudication-basis allowlist supplied to validation; path/name/content heuristics cannot self-authorize it

relation_record.id_rule: relation_id = 'REL-' + full 64-lowercase-hex SHA-256 of canonical identity_payload
supersession_rules: superseded relation must exist in an ancestor segment
superseded relation must be currently active at the point of replay
successor must preserve source_ref relation_type and target_ref exactly
relation_status basis_ref and supersedes_relation_ref may change
one active relation may have at most one direct successor
later correction must supersede the current active successor, not an older ancestor

registry_segment.events_rule: new events only; array strictly sorted by event_id; duplicate-free
registry_segment.relations_rule: new relations only; array strictly sorted by relation_id; duplicate-free
registry_segment.id_rule: registry_id = 'RGS-' + full 64-lowercase-hex SHA-256 of canonical identity_payload
replay_rules: exactly one genesis must exist once initialized
each parent may have at most one child
the complete validated graph must form one linear chain
the unique tip is the derived current head
event_id and relation_id may appear only once across the entire chain
child omission never deletes ancestor records
forks are never auto-merged or auto-selected

PASS.meaning: technical registry integrity PASS within this contract only
requires: all current segment files parse under exact schema
complete chain resolves to exactly one genesis and one tip
all decisive references required for technical validation resolve
all ADJUDICATED relations have separately human-authorized basis

BLOCKED.meaning: cannot safely determine a technically usable registry state because required external identity/authority/chain resolution is unavailable or ambiguous
examples: registry fork or no unique head
ADJUDICATED relation without separately authorized adjudication basis

test_cases: canonical hash is invariant to input object key insertion order
canonical JSON uses UTF-8 sort_keys separators comma/colon ensure_ascii false with no BOM
duplicate JSON object key is rejected
JSON number inside an identity-bearing payload is rejected
identical event core produces identical full-length EVENT_ID
source_refs and evidence_refs must be lexicographically sorted and duplicate-free
identical relation core produces identical full-length RELATION_ID
missing or syntactically invalid BASIS_REF fails
ADJUDICATED without separately human-authorized basis is BLOCKED
supersedes ref must resolve to an ancestor relation
supersession must preserve source_ref relation_type and target_ref
same prior relation cannot have two active direct successors
unresolvable git blob or commit reference is BLOCKED
valid genesis has null parent and becomes sole initial head
missing parent registry segment is BLOCKED
segment filename must exactly match REGISTRY_ID
events array must be strictly sorted by event_id and duplicate-free
relations array must be strictly sorted by relation_id and duplicate-free
event id already present in ancestor chain fails even if byte-equivalent
relation id already present in ancestor chain fails even if byte-equivalent
two children of one parent produce REGISTRY_FORK and BLOCKED
one fully resolvable linear chain has one derived head and may PASS technical validation
omission of an ancestor event from a child segment does not delete the ancestor event
tampering with a persisted segment changes its content-bound registry identity and fails
event references inside the same segment may resolve after event-id validation
relation refs to relations created in the same segment are forbidden
validator output cannot claim registry completeness pristine status scientific support or independence
validator output cannot compute or assert N_budget or N_famille
retrospective occurred_at does not imply earlier durable knowledge; chain/Git ancestry governs persistence order
RESERVED_FOR and CLASSIFIED_BY can use a non-event SOURCE_REF such as immutable git_blob
all four adopted relation types are representable without adding a fifth relation type

implementation_boundary.next_step_if_separately_authorized: create frozen breaker first, demonstrate expected RED against absent implementation, then authorize minimal implementation separately
